question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution:
The correct answer is '**a whimper**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase “not with a bang, but a whimper” originates from TS Eliot’s poem "The Hollow Men" and is commonly used to describe an anticlimactic or quiet ending.
 
• In the context of the passage, it implies that while child prodigies show early promise, their impact on history tends to fade rather than culminate in something grand.
 
• "**A whimper**" fits best as it conveys the idea of an underwhelming or unremarkable conclusion.
 
• Other options do not fit the idiomatic phrase or the intended meaning of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "An impalpable" (अस्पृश्य) means something that cannot be touched or grasped, which does not fit in the context of describing an ending.
 
• "A reconcile" (समाधान) is grammatically incorrect and does not fit the context.
 
• "An indomitable" (अजय) means impossible to subdue, which contradicts the idea of fading away quietly.
